expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses the bug and gives a minimal fix or hint, not a rewrite of the project
expectations.evidence: Diagnoses the bug: 'git's hash-object doesn't hash the raw content — it hashes the object header `<type> <size>\0` + content' and gives a minimal fix 'sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(data) + data).hexdigest()' plus a 3-line hash_object function — a hint-sized fix, not a project rewrite.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: The answer ends with explanatory bullets ('两点说明：- zlib 压缩与哈希值无关…- 同样的头部格式也适用于其他类型…'), not a checkpoint. The only commands ('echo -n "hello" | git hash-object --stdin…') are introduced as the agent's own demo ('Let me do a quick demo') and reported as already executed ('已在上方验证'), with no closing 'run this and expect X' instruction to the learner.

expectations.text: B3: Explains that the hash must be computed over the header `blob <size>\0` + content (not the raw data), before compression
expectations.evidence: 'it hashes the object header `<type> <size>\0` + content. So the correct computation is `sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(data) + data).hexdigest()`' and 'zlib 压缩与哈希值无关——先进行哈希，然后 `zlib.compress(full)`' — header+content before compression, explicitly.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only command run: 'printf 'hello' | git hash-object --stdin; python3 -c …' — read-only verification, no install commands (no brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install), FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0), nothing outside the workspace.
